# Plan: Build the opening environment and terminal

## Design

Source context: `index.html` has `#app` and loads `src/main.ts`; `three` is in `package.json`; `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts` serves the build under `/signal-lost/`; `.swarm/architecture.md` names the `app`, `render`, `terminal`, and `input` modules.

- `src/app/scenes.ts`: DOM-free `createSceneManager()`. A `Scene` has `mount(): void` and `dispose(): void`. `show(scene)` disposes the current scene before mounting the next one; `dispose()` tears down the current one. Pure, unit-tested.
- `src/app/opening.ts`: opening scene. Prints the design's SIGNAL RECEIVED text line by line, then the prompt. Enter or a click at any time moves on. Removes its listeners on dispose.
- `src/app/hub.ts`: boot sequence and terminal hub. Prints the OBSERVER NETWORK boot text, then a numbered tool menu from a `Tool[]` list. Tools are `{ id, label, run }`. This WorkUnit ships only real ones (`STATUS`, `HELP`); later WorkUnits add theirs. No placeholder entries.
- `src/terminal/terminal.ts`: DOM terminal. `print(lines)`, `menu(items)`, and a command input. Output goes in a `role="log"` `aria-live="polite"` element as real text. Menu items are buttons, also chosen by typing the number or name.
- `src/render/environment.ts`: Three.js scene, loaded by dynamic import so text appears before the 3D code does. Starfield `Points`, a flat-shaded low-poly icosahedron with a ring, a moving analyzer sweep line, low-resolution rendering with pixelated CSS scaling, vertex snapping by `onBeforeCompile`. `createEnvironment(canvas, { motion })` returns `{ start, stop, setMotion, dispose }`, or throws when WebGL is unavailable. Rendering stops when the document is hidden and on `stop`/`dispose`, which also disposes geometries, materials and the renderer. `motion: false` renders one still frame.
- `src/main.ts`: bootstraps. If the environment throws, it sets `document.body.dataset.render = 'fallback'` and shows a CSS-only static starfield; otherwise `'webgl'`. The game continues either way.
- `src/style.css`: CRT bezel, amber phosphor, subtle scanlines and vignette, and periodic interference as a CSS animation on an overlay. System monospace stack, because no font asset is in the repo.

Opening and boot text are fixed interface text in `src/app/text.ts`. Story content starts in the Episode 000 WorkUnit.

## Files

New: `src/app/{scenes,opening,hub,text}.ts`, `src/terminal/terminal.ts`, `src/render/environment.ts`, `src/style.css`, `tests/unit/scenes.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts`. Changed: `src/main.ts`, `index.html` only if the stylesheet link needs it, `tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts` (the old text expectation still applies), `playwright.config.ts` (add a software WebGL launch flag so tests can exercise the real renderer).

## Edge cases

- Enter pressed before the opening finishes still boots.
- WebGL failing at context creation shows the fallback with no uncaught error.
- A dynamic-import or render failure also uses the fallback.
- Resizing updates the renderer size.

## Out of scope

Puzzles, audio, persistence, settings UI.

# Test plan

| Acceptance criterion | Verification | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opening shows starfield, rotating object, sweep, interference and the text, ending in the prompt | `tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts`: text and prompt visible, `body[data-render=webgl]`, canvas has non-blank pixels, interference overlay present. Source inspection of `environment.ts` for the scene elements. | Developer on host; CI `Browser tests` |
| Enter or click boots into a terminal with a tool menu | `opening.spec.ts`, once with Enter and once with click, then a menu button works and a typed command works | Developer on host; CI |
| WebGL failure shows a styled fallback and stays playable | `opening.spec.ts` forces `getContext` to return null by init script: `data-render=fallback`, no page errors, boot still works | Developer on host; CI |
| Lifecycle mounts and disposes scenes, rendering stops when not needed | `npx vitest run tests/unit/scenes.test.ts`; source inspection of `stop`/`dispose` and the visibility handling | Developer; tester inspects |
| Browser tests cover opening, boot, fallback under the subpath | `fixtures.ts` returns 404 outside `/signal-lost/`; `opening.spec.ts` uses it | CI |

## Roles

- **Developer:** runs focused commands above and `npm run lint`. Browser specs run on the host session, as sandboxes cannot start Chromium (`.swarm/rules/lessons.md`).
- **Tester:** independently inspects source against the criteria, reuses applicable passing results, repeats only for relevant changes, failures, or unresolved coverage.
- **Coordinator:** alone runs the complete required policy. The `Browser tests` workflow on the PR is the browser evidence.

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED

The proposed areas and dependencies fit ISSUE-5, but the handoff needs the revisions below before implementation.

| Contract area | Audit | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opening visuals and exact text (AC1) | Visual components are planned; the claimed design copy is not verifiable. | PLAN.md references “the design's SIGNAL RECEIVED text” and “OBSERVER NETWORK boot text”; docs/game-design.md contains neither sequence nor the final join prompt. |
| Keyboard/pointer boot and terminal (AC2) | Covered by opening/hub separation, DOM buttons, command input, and separate Enter/click browser journeys. | PLAN.md app/terminal design; TEST_PLAN.md AC2 row. |
| Styled, playable WebGL fallback (AC3) | Failure injection and fallback styling are covered; verification currently stops at boot. | TEST_PLAN.md AC3 row says “boot still works,” while AC2 exercises menu and commands only in the normal journey. |
| Lifecycle and rendering shutdown (AC4) | Scene manager API is clear, but renderer ownership and transition cleanup are unspecified. | PLAN.md separates createSceneManager from createEnvironment without describing their connection; TEST_PLAN.md names a lifecycle test but leaves renderer shutdown to inspection. |
| Pages browser coverage (AC5) | Appropriate production-build fixture and CI ownership. | tests/e2e/fixtures.ts serves only /signal-lost/; playwright.config.ts uses that baseURL and production-build setup. |
| Low resolution, restrained effects, readable DOM output | Covered by flat shading, low-resolution canvas, CSS effects, role=log and aria-live=polite. | PLAN.md render, CSS and terminal sections. |
| Scope and protected paths | No protected edits, puzzles, audio, backend, or new dependencies proposed. | PLAN.md file list and exclusions; package.json already includes three. |
| Validation responsibilities | Correctly reserves complete required policy for coordinator and browser execution for host/CI. | TEST_PLAN.md Roles; SYSTEM_PROMPT.md sandbox limitations. |

## Required revisions

1. Resolve the missing text source. Specify the opening sequence and boot copy, including the required final `PRESS ENTER TO JOIN THE NETWORK`, or cite an existing verifiable source for them. Identify any newly authored copy as a proposal rather than existing design text. Keep fixed interface labels in code, and place any narrative copy in content/ as required by the conventions. Add any needed content file to the file list and assert the agreed sequence in the browser test. No changes to mystery facts are authorized.

2. Define lifecycle ownership across main.ts, opening.ts, hub.ts and environment.ts: which scene needs the renderer, who starts/stops/disposes it on transitions, and who cleans up timers/listeners. Address a dynamic import resolving after its owning scene is disposed so it cannot restart unused rendering. Make scenes.test.ts assertions explicit for mount order, replacement disposal, and final disposal; add a focused, DOM-free scheduling/ownership test (using injected or fake renderer callbacks) proving rendering stops when no longer needed. State how visibility handling resumes only an active renderer. This should remain a small extension of the proposed design, not a new framework.

3. Complete the reproducible verification handoff. Extend the forced-WebGL-failure journey through a menu action and typed command, checking readable DOM output and no page errors. Give the browser command, such as `npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts`, with host/Browser tests CI ownership; do not make sandbox implementation depend on launching Chromium. Specify source-inspection checks for rotation, sweep movement, periodic interference and low-resolution rendering, since a nonblank canvas and overlay presence alone do not establish those behaviors.

## Evidence and handoff

Verified the plan's existing-source claims against index.html, src/main.ts, package.json, .swarm/architecture.md, playwright.config.ts, tests/e2e/fixtures.ts and tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts. The current app is only SIGNAL RECEIVED text; planned modules are proposals, not existing implementations. REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md repeats the current design and test plan and contains no separate previous review or unmerged lesson that resolves these gaps. Sandbox/browser lessons in SYSTEM_PROMPT.md remain applicable.

The developer owns app/renderer/terminal implementation and focused unit/lint evidence. The tester independently checks the acceptance mapping and reuses applicable passing results. The existing Browser tests workflow supplies browser evidence; the coordinator owns final trusted-base checks. No implementation tests were run for this plan audit.
